questions.q:
What is the work function of the metal if the light of wavelength $4000\overset{o}{A}$ generates photoelectrons of velocity $6 \times {10}^{5}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ from it?

(Mass of electron $= 9 \times {10}^{- 31}kg$, velocity of light $= 3 \times {10}^{8}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$, Planck's constant $= 6 .626 \times {10}^{- 34}Js$, Charge of electron $= 6 .626 \times {10}^{- 34}Js$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{hc}{λ} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda0} + \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2}$

$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda0} = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{6.626 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{4000 \times {10}^{- 10}} - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(9.1 \times {10}^{- 31}\right) \times {\left(6 \times {10}^{5}\right)}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{6.626 \times 3 \times {10}^{- 19}}{4} - \dfrac{9.1 \times 6 \times 6}{2} \times {10}^{- 21}$

$= 4.97 \times {10}^{- 19} - 1.64 \times {10}^{- 19}$

$= 3.33 \times {10}^{- 19}$ Joule

Work function \left(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda0}\right) = \dfrac{3 .33 \times {10}^{- 19}}{1 .6 \times {10}^{- 19}} = 2 .08 \approx 2 .1 eV

questions.q: Maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in shell with $n = 4$ are:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The maximum number of electrons that could be present in a shell is given by the rule 2n2.

Where n is the shell number.

The first shell K shell can accommodate a maximum of 2 electrons ($2 \times {1}^{2} = 2$).

The second shell L shell can accommodate a maximum of 8 electrons ($2 \times {2}^{2} = 8$).

Likewise, the 4th shell named N can accommodate a maximum of 32 electrons ($2 \times {4}^{2} = 2 \times 16 = 32$).

For hydrogen atom :&

questions.q:
Which of the following pair is not isoelectronic species?
(Atomic numbers& $Sm = 62; Er = 68; Yb = 70; Lu = 71; Eu = 63; Tb = 65; Tm = 69$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Isoelectronic species are those which have the same number of electrons.

The number of electrons in an ion is given by the atomic number minus the charge of the ion.

For $Sm^{2+}$, the number of electrons is $62 - 2 = 60$. For $Eu^{3+}$, the number of electrons is $63 - 3 = 60$. These are isoelectronic.

For $Yb^{2+}$, the number of electrons is $70 - 2 = 68$. For $Lu^{3+}$, the number of electrons is $71 - 3 = 68$. These are isoelectronic.

For $Eu^{2+}$, the number of electrons is $63 - 2 = 61$. For $Tb^{4+}$, the number of electrons is $65 - 4 = 61$. These are isoelectronic.

For $Tb^{2+}$, the number of electrons is $65 - 2 = 63$. For $Tm^{4+}$, the number of electrons is $69 - 4 = 65$. Since they have a different number of electrons, they are not isoelectronic. !

questions.q: The energy of an electron in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom is& $- 2 . 18 \times {10}^{- 18}J$ Its energy in the third Bohr orbit is_______ .
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The energy of an electron in the $n$-th Bohr orbit of a hydrogen atom is given by the expression:

$E_n = \dfrac{E_1}{n^2}$

where $E_1$ is the energy of the electron in the first Bohr orbit.

Given $E_1 = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \text{ J}$.

For the third Bohr orbit, $n = 3$.

Substituting the value of $n$ into the expression for $E_n$:

$E_3 = \dfrac{E_1}{3^2}$

$E_3 = \dfrac{1}{9} E_1$

Therefore, the energy of the electron in the third Bohr orbit is $\dfrac{1}{9}\text{th}$ of its energy in the first Bohr orbit. ~

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength $(\lambda)$ associated with a photoelectron varies with the frequency $(v)$ of the incident radiation as,\left[v_{0}\right.$ is threshold frequency]:$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
According to de-Broglie wavelength equation, \lambda=$\frac{h}{m v} \Rightarrow \lambda \propto \frac{1}{v}$According to photoelectric effect,
hv-hv_{0}=$\frac{1}{2}$mv^{2} ; v-v_{0}=$\frac{1}{2}=\frac{mv^{2}}{ h}$
v-v_{0} \propto \mathrmv^{2}
v \propto\left($v-v_{0}\right)^{1 / 2}
\therefore \quad \lambda \propto $\frac{1}{\left(v-v_{0}\right)^{1 / 2}}$
$

questions.q:
Heat treatment of muscular pain involves radiation of wavelength of about 900 nm . Which spectral line of H atom is suitable for this?
Given : Rydberg constant $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=10^5 \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}, \mathrm{~h}=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~s}, \mathrm{c}=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ )
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \lambda=900 \mathrm{~nm} \quad \text { H-atom }(\mathrm{Z}=1) \\
& =9 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~cm} \\
& \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=10^5 \mathrm{~cm}^{-1} \\
& \text { Ryderg eq. }=\frac{1}{\lambda}=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \mathrm{Z}^2 \times\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\lambda \times \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{9 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~cm} \times 10^5 \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}}=\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}=\frac{1}{9}
\end{aligned}$ It is possible when $\mathrm{n}_1=3, \mathrm{n}_2=\infty$
Possible series : $\infty \rightarrow 3$

Maximum number of emission lines

& $= \dfrac{\Delta n\left(\Delta n + 1\right)}{2}\Delta n = {n}_{2} - {n}_{1}{n}_{2} = 5{n}_{1} = 1$
